info.description:
Sparta screens calls with an AI assistant that always says it is an AI, refuses requests for protected information and
explains every decision. Errors share one envelope: `{"error": {"code", "message", "trace_id", "details"}}`.

**Development mode** has no credentials; clients must show a *Development identity* banner (`/system/status`).
**Provider callbacks** (`/webhooks/*`, `/media/*`) are not part of this document.
info.title: Sparta API

put.description:
The AI disclosure is not part of the profile: it cannot be switched off. `use_personal_voice` is refused (409)
unless the voice is `ready` and the feature is enabled.

post.description: Runs the real conversation engine on `sample_text` without creating a call or storing anything.

get.description: Sensitive actions (deletions, exports, list changes, preference changes). Identifiers only, never content.

delete.description: Remove all of the owner's call content (calls stay as records without transcripts).

post.description:
Start a call through the configured telephony provider.

Real providers create calls when the provider delivers them, so this answers 409 `unsupported_by_provider` unless
the provider is the simulator.

Transcribe an uploaded clip in memory and run it as a caller turn.

With the simulator STT there is no acoustic model: send `transcript_hint`, otherwise this is 422 `stt_unavailable`.

delete.description:
Remove the transcript, translations, live events, summary, risk explanation, claims and any feedback notes.

The call record stays (time, duration, status, final risk level and category, blocked/trusted flags).

post.description: 409 `unsupported_by_provider` when the active telephony provider cannot do this; `CallDetail.capabilities` says which controls are real.
409 `unsupported_by_provider` when the active telephony provider cannot do this; `CallDetail.capabilities` says which controls are real.

get.description: Everything stored about one call (owner only). Includes the transcript while it is retained.

post.description: Idempotent per call and kind: repeating a kind updates the note of the existing record.
Caller barge-in: stops the assistant's playback and keeps the conversation state.
Emit a `transcript.partial` event only (no pipeline run): live captions while the caller is still speaking.

get.description: Sanitised diagnostic report: identifiers, states, timings and codes. No transcript text or numbers.

post.description: Fire one silence timeout (what the timer does on a real call).
409 `unsupported_by_provider` when the active telephony provider cannot do this; `CallDetail.capabilities` says which controls are real.

get.description: Protection status, the next useful action, today's counters and the calls that need the owner.

post.description: A single-use WebSocket ticket for all of the owner's calls, or for one call (`call_id`).

put.description: Replaces the owner's preferences. Unknown fields are rejected; languages and retention are validated.

get.description: Medium and high risk calls with the signal codes that triggered them. Never transcript text.
What Sparta refuses and why, in the terms the policy itself uses (no hidden rules).
`fingerprint_salt` is the base64 HMAC key the device uses to fingerprint numbers. Treat it as a secret.

post.description:
Records what the device decided as a `screening_only` call. Idempotent on `client_event_id`: native screening
cannot answer a call or hear its audio, so such a call has no transcript.

With `scenario_id` and `autoplay`, the scripted caller is played server-side with its gaps, and every step is
streamed over the live socket.

get.description: Which adapters are active and which could be: a provider that is not configured says what is missing.

post.description:
Deterministic replay in an isolated container (virtual clock, in-memory database): the same input yields the same
`checksum`. Nothing is written to the owner's call history.

get.description:
Public and free of personal data. Clients must show a "Development identity" banner when `dev_banner` is true,
and must show whether telephony is real or simulated.

post.description:
Records consent. The status becomes `pending_provider_approval`: the voice provider's approval cannot be
completed inside Sparta.

get.description: Liveness: the process is up. Never touches dependencies, so a database outage does not restart the service.

Prometheus text. Off unless `SPARTA_EXPOSE_METRICS=true`; counters and timings only (no personal data), but still
restrict the route to your monitoring network.

Readiness: the hard dependencies answer: the database (reachable, schema present, migrations at the version this
code expects) and shared state. A new revision therefore takes no traffic until `python -m sparta migrate` has run.
A degraded telephony provider is reported but does not make the service unready, because the owner can still use
everything else.
